overview: This Senate resolution designates November 20, 2025, as National Rural Health Day. It notes that more than 66 million Americans live in rural areas, where people face shortages of doctors, long travel distances and higher rates of being uninsured, and that many rural hospitals have closed or are losing money. It celebrates rural health care providers and the communities they serve and states a commitment to improving health care access and affordability in rural areas. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on November 19, 2025. It is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
for: Supporters say the resolution draws attention to the real struggles of rural hospitals and patients and honors the health workers who serve them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not provide any funding or policy change to keep rural hospitals open.
